svg.text: at 20 °C. Shrink goes on the CAVITY, not here
cut on the cross centre-line, so the slot reads full depth
cut on the cable centre-line -- the FFC exit is
0.50 wide at the seat floor and 3.50 at z = 0
section at z = 0.30, just above the lead-in chamfer
The display-seat floor, looking down +Z (as V3).
Thin outline = the seat floor, the face it is cut into.
The pocket ceiling as V4 projects it (looking up -Z).
Same stamp, same depth, TURNED 180° -- not mirrored. It
reads normally when the part is flipped over front-to-back,
which is how you turn one over to look at its underside.
1. Axes are the model's own (OpenSCAD): +X right, +Y
back, +Z up, origin at the centre of the MX stem on the
moulding face (z = 0). Each view carries the pair it
build123d. The STEP is the shape reference; THIS DRAWING
3. CRITICAL MX slot 4.05 x 1.10 ±0.03, R0.30 corner
fillets (V7). Gauge against a real MX switch stem, not
by CMM alone. Per the fit table our slot is deliberately
tighter than Cherry's published keycap slot; the four
relief bulges are what make that work.
4. CRITICAL The transparent relegendable cap is an
off-the-shelf POS part, so that mating dimension is a
hard datum set by a supplier we do not control. Confirm
5. Draft, measured off the model: outer body 11.6°,
inside pocket 18.4°. ZERO DRAFT on the display seat
(12.2 x 12.1 x 1.1 deep) and on its cable relief (V9) --
confirm release at first article rather than meeting it
6. Slot draft 0.08° on the flats, 0.31° at the arm tips,
opening downward: the core pin withdraws the right way,
but with very little relief. Polish along the arms. The
slot runs from the moulding face to z = 5.83 -- through
the boss and on into the cap floor (V5).
7. The inner chamfer in V4 (33.0°) is switch-body
clearance, not cosmetic -- it is what stops the cap
fouling a bulky switch. Do not flatten it to simplify
8. The three 0.40 x 3.00 x 0.30 tabs standing 0.20 proud
(+Y and ±X, V3) are a FUNCTIONAL feature: they are what
makes the clear keycap click on properly. They are NOT a
3D-printing artefact and must NOT be removed.
9. Stamp "β S" = revision + profile, 0.30 deep, zero
draft, in TWO places: the display-seat floor (V8) and
the pocket ceiling (V10). The second is TURNED 180°, not
mirrored -- it reads normally when the part is flipped
over front-to-back. Drawn in V10; do not infer it.
Revision character is U+03B2 GREEK SMALL LETTER BETA --
the moulded part is deliberately β where the 3D-printed
prototypes are α, so the two are told apart by eye.
Carry it on a REPLACEABLE INSERT in the cavity rather
than cut into the block: a revision change is then a
plug swap, not a tool edit. Font Noto Sans Bold,
10. The slot lead-in opens to 4.61 x 4.61 at z = 0 over
0.30 mm (~46°). Cherry publishes no lead-in dimension,
so this one is ours; keep it, it is what lets the cap
11. GATE AND EJECTORS are the moulder's choice, but they
must NOT land on the MX slot or its lead-in, the display
seat floor or cable relief, the three click tabs, or the
moulding face (z = 0). A side wall (±X) clear of the
tabs is the obvious place, feeding toward the stem boss
-- the thickest section. The 3D-printed prototypes were
sprued from Ø1.5 runners on that same wall, so it
already tolerates a witness mark. Mark the positions
chosen on the tooling drawing and send it back.
12. Surface: tool polish on the slot and the stem bore;
the outer faces may carry the standard texture. No flash
permitted on the slot, the tabs or the seat floor.
MX SLOT vs CHERRY'S PUBLISHED KEYCAP SPEC
Sources: Cherry's keycap slot spec via deskthority / telcontar.net. The stem's own cross is
ASYMMETRIC and Cherry's uniform 1.17 slot already interferes ~0.07 on two sides; ours is
tighter still, so the fit rests on the relief bulges. Verify on a moulded first article.
